utterances.text: Sir, you informed us that your brother was witnessing the killing of your father and you also told us that the soldier said, "One of you must die." So my question is who made the choice who will be killed, your father or your brother? Was it the soldier or who?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN NASIC
utterances.text: My father.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we managed to finish with your testimony today, as you see. And that will enable you to return back home earlier than you probably were expecting. You will be attended to by the usher, who will escort you out of this courtroom but before you leave it is my duty as the Presiding Judge on my own behalf, on behalf of the other two Judges in this Trial Chamber as well as the Tribunal to thank you for having accepted to come and give evidence. You may now leave and I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Trbojevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, may my associate be allowed to object to interpretation that was recorded in the transcript, in order for me not to create the confusion, she will explain in her good English what term was used instead of what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No problem from the Prosecution either?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. JEVTOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. If we go on page 43, line 2, we will see that the word "cleansed" has been used, and when this word was used --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. 43? Line 2?

utterances.speaker: MS. JEVTOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and later on too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. JEVTOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The word "cleansed" was used. Then the translation when going from the B/C/S booth was "ethnic cleansing" in the language that I was listening to. The witness was talking about what we used to earlier previous days translate as "mopping up" or "sweeping up" or "cleaning." And we have the same occurrence on page 67, line 3. That is all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour this is something that probably could have been cleared up with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In fact if the witness is still here, we will bring him back in, usher? Where is she? Ms. Gustin, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The usher will be with the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. JEVTOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sir, before you leave again because we had a small problem. At a certain point, during your testimony, you were being asked this series of questions and your answers were as follows and now I will explain to you what the problem is. You were asked, "And when you weren't at your aunt's house, where were you?" And you said, "We were hiding in the woods, the same woods." And then you were asked, "Approximately how many people were hiding in the woods were you?" And you answered, "During the first day we had small groups of some 10, 20, 30 people there." And then were you asked, "How long did you stay in the woods for?" And you said, "About a month. To a month and a half." Question: "Of the people that were in the woods, how many of them were armed?" And you said, "I don't know. After the villages were cleansed." Now, what did you mean by the word "cleansed" and what word exactly did you use?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, can you repeat the question. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes the question was this, you were asked of the people that were in the woods how many of them were armed and you said, I don't know after the villages were cleansed, the neighbouring villages such as Biscani, Rakovcani, et cetera, there were some 300 to 400 civilians. You are reported here to have used the word "cleansed" after the villages were cleansed. What word did you use and what did you mean by that word?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what they called it, cleansing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What did you mean by it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. That simply is what they called it, cleansing of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who called it like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Cleansing of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Terrain, villages. This is what our people would say, they started cleansing the village. Because that word was used quite a lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you ever heard the word ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I've heard about that word, but in this case, no reference was made to ethnic cleansing. This was just plain cleansing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What we call mopping up as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it the equivalent of mopping up? Cleansing means mopping up? Have you ever heard of the term "mopping up"? I don't know how that is being translated to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I truly don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I want from you is also another clarification. Later on you said, you referred to -- you were asked to answer a question about the death, the killing of your father and I myself asked you to confirm whether the killing took place on the 21st of July or not and you said, "I'm sorry, I'm not sure about the date but it was a day when Biscani was cleansed." Also you mean cleansed, the terrain being cleansed, and not ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Same word, same meaning. It was not ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. You may now leave. Sorry for having brought you back to the hall. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anything?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: First of all, I think Judge Janu may want the audio-visual directors to take a photo of her in her elevated status. We have a list of the witnesses for the Bosanski Novi municipality starting around the 23rd of January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Incidentally we would also require, if possible, that you enter a note showing the sequence in which these -- the next municipalities will be dealt with. My staff requires it and I think also the Defence would find it extremely useful.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour if I understand Ms. Korner well, we will be completing the municipalities in the order they appear in the pre-trial brief, although we have dropped a couple of those municipalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But again, I mean Ms. Korner had confirmed that orally. It's not that I doubt her word but I think for the proper conduct of the proceedings if we have this document between now and when we commence the Christmas recess, I think that would be quite useful at least for my staff if not for the Defence. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour we will provide you with that before we begin again on the 13th of January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I think this is the last time we are sitting before the holidays, and I am taking this opportunity on my behalf and on behalf of my two colleagues to wish you all the very best for the festive season, those who celebrate Christmas and those who -- and the new year, and those who don't. And we will look forward to resuming our works on the 12th of -- 13th of January. So our greetings. To you as well, Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1.47 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 13th day of January, 2003.
